articles.content: STORY: From what happened when Grok went rogue, to a vicious battle for talent in Silicon Valley, this is AI Weekly.Grok is in trouble again.Elon Musk’s xAI had to remove posts by its chatbot, after complaints that they contained antisemitic content and praise for Adolf Hitler.xAI moved to delete the posts, and said it could quickly update the AI model where there was evidence it had been badly trained.A court also blocked some Grok content in Turkey, after authorities said the bot had made insulting remarks about country President Tayyip Erdogan.The war for talent is getting hot in Silicon Valley, and it’s Meta fanning the flames.Ilya Sutskever is having to take over as boss of his startup Safe Superintelligence, after losing chief executive Daniel Gross to the Facebook parent firm.Bloomberg News says Apple has also lost its top AI models exec to Mark Zuckerberg’s company.Meta has been hiring aggressively in a bid to match OpenAI and other rivals.A bot sowed confusion for diplomats, when someone used an AI-generated voice to impersonate U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.The person reportedly contacted three foreign ministers and two U.S. officials, sometimes leaving voice notes.Their intent was to gain access to information or accounts, according to a diplomatic cable seen by Reuters.The EU isn’t backing down on its new AI rules.Brussels has dismissed appeals by Meta, Alphabet and other big names to delay the regulations for years.Now the European Commission says there is no option to “stop the clock” on the rules, which aim to set guardrails for AI.But it says it will takes steps to simplify the measures, including for small firms.And Microsoft is cutting jobs to help pay for bots.Some 4% of roles face the chop at the Windows maker, as it tries to find savings amid massive investment in AI.It’s pledged about $80 billion in capital spending this year, taking a bite out of profit margins.
